title: Insert a retaining fork into a shaft groove
context: Captive shafts need a retaining part inserted from the side below a head. One arm stabilises the loose fixture while the other feeds a rigid fork into a narrow axial groove. Both tines must pass the shaft centre.
scoring: The episode scores zero if the fixture ever moves more than 5 mm or the fork falls more than 5 mm below the tabletop. Fork tilt and yaw must each be below 5 degrees. A lifted fork earns 0.25. A partly inserted fork earns 0.5 when x is within 6 mm of 280 mm and z is within 5 mm of 814 mm and y lies between negative 82.5 mm and negative 47.5 mm. Full seating needs the fork centre within 4 mm on every axis of x 280 mm and y negative 47.5 mm and z 814 mm. Translation must be below 8 mm per second and rotation below 0.1 radians per second. This earns 0.75. Both grippers open beyond 35 mm raises this to 1.0. Full success must hold for 2 seconds. All other outcomes score zero.
fidelity: All solids are rigid printed PA12 polymer. The fork has two actual tines and an open slot. The shaft has an 8 mm high groove below its square head. The tines are 6 mm thick. The raised handling tab provides gripper access. Contact offsets are 0.25 mm for the compound solids. Small physical locators constrain the loose fixture. There is no elastic snap fit or powered motion.
instruction: Hold the grey shaft fixture still with one arm. With the other arm slide the blue retaining fork sideways into the shaft groove below its square head. Both tines must reach beyond the shaft centre. Release both grippers. Keep the fixture within 5 mm of its starting position. All equipment is unpowered.
setup: Use the bimanual YAM station with the tabletop at z 747.5 mm. x points forward. y points left. z points up. Every part is printed PA12 polymer. scene_inventory.json lists every object and every solid with exact dimensions and initial positions in metres and masses in kilograms. Object positions use the world frame. Solid positions use their body frame. Joint anchors and limits are listed with the articulated object. The setup image shows this fixed layout. All joint positions start at zero.
run_limit: 500 control steps at 20 Hz. This is 25 seconds of control time.
reset_notes: Restore every object to the starting pose in scene_inventory.json and every joint to zero. Nothing is consumed. Use one epoch with seed 0 and object_jitter=0.
scores: Both uploaded videos show the same scripted demo with score 1.0. No model score is claimed.
